answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150-157, mi_rank(score) maps the maintainability index to a grade with `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. Score > 19 gives 'A'. 9 < score <= 19 gives 'B'. Score <= 9 gives 'C'. This matches the docstring at lines 153-155. At the boundaries, 19 gives B and 9 gives C, so both thresholds are inclusive on the lower grade. The arithmetic-on-booleans trick is terse. Review should add explicit boundary tests for 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01, plus a check for float and NaN inputs. radon/visitors.py is where the raw metrics are computed that feed mi_visit, so review it for how the inputs to the score are produced. radon/complexity.py has a similar rank function for cyclomatic complexity, so check it for threshold consistency. radon/raw.py needs only a brief look.
